'''Boris Z. Shapiro''' (born 1957, [[Moscow]], [[Soviet Union]]) is a [[Russia]]n-[[Sweden|Swedish]] mathematician, whose research concerns [[differential equation]]s, [[commutative algebra]] and [[Schubert calculus]]. The Shapiro–Shapiro conjecture (or simply the Shapiro conjecture) was named after Michael Shapiro and him<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://math.boisestate.edu/~zteitler/statements/ResearchStatement.pdf |title=Archived copy |access-date=2015-04-28 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150526110152/http://math.boisestate.edu/~zteitler/statements/ResearchStatement.pdf |archive-date=2015-05-26 |url-status=dead }}</ref> (it is now the well-known Mukhin–Tarasov–[[Alexander Varchenko|Varchenko]] theorem<ref>{{Cite arXiv |eprint = 0911.2039|last1 = Purbhoo|first1 = Kevin|title = Reality and transversality for Schubert calculus in OG(n,2n+1)|class = math.AG|year = 2009}}</ref>).

Shapiro enrolled in the PhD program at [[Moscow State University]], [[Soviet Union]] in 1985 as a student of [[Vladimir Arnold]], but his thesis defense was rejected by the examining committee. He then defended the same thesis at [[Stockholm University]], [[Sweden]] in 1990, and was awarded his PhD. He became the most prolific PhD student of Arnold, in terms of academic descendance.<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=20563}}</ref> He has been a professor at Stockholm University since 1993.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.spms.ntu.edu.sg/mas/Colloquium/2012/Colloquium%20_%20Prof%20Boris%20Shapiro.pdf |title=Archived copy |access-date=2015-04-28 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150526090542/http://www.spms.ntu.edu.sg/mas/Colloquium/2012/Colloquium%20_%20Prof%20Boris%20Shapiro.pdf |archive-date=2015-05-26 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>According to [[Google Scholar]], as of 10 June 2025, Shapiro's works have been cited 2314 times, and his [[h-index]] is 23: https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=wGwg1L4AAAAJ</ref>

==Selected papers==
*A. Postnikov, B. Shapiro, "[https://www.ams.org/journals/tran/2004-356-08/S0002-9947-04-03547-0/ Trees, parking functions, syzygies, and deformations of monomial ideals]", ''[[Transactions of the American Mathematical Society]]'' 356 (8), pp.&nbsp;3109–3142.
*B. Shapiro, M. Shapiro, A. Vainshtein, "Ramified Coverings of S² With One Degenerate Branching Point And Enumeration of Edge-Ordered Graphs", ''Proceedings of the 8th [[International Conference on Formal Power Series and Algebraic Combinatorics]]'', 1996, pp.&nbsp;421–426.
*B. Shapiro, J. Borcea, P. Brändén, "Pólya-Schur master theorems for circular domains and their boundaries", ''[[Annals of Mathematics]]'', pp. 465–492 from Volume 170 (2009).
